note: The importer opens the in-memory fuzzer input so the first bytes of the candidate control format detection.
The input bytes 3DMO make the generic memory import path select the M3D importer despite no filename hint.
The selected importer stores exactly fileSize input bytes in a vector that becomes the backing container passed to the M3D SDK.
For the candidate, the embedded binary header length equals the actual 8 byte fileSize, so parsing continues.

code: m3d_ = m3d_load(const_cast<unsigned char *>(buffer.data()), nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);
note: The vector data pointer is transferred to m3d_load without also providing buffer.size(), so the callee has no bound before probing data past the 8 byte file.
With an 8 byte input, data + 8 is one byte past the vector contents; the M3D_CHUNKMAGIC macro reads from it, producing the container-overflow read.
